A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToM-SWE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, a ToM-model cost comparison, simulator validation, and a three-week study with 17 developers.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports a preliminary single-agent comparison and further analyses of task resolution versus satisfaction.

M1.justification: The dual-agent architecture, three-tier memory, consultation and update procedures, retrieval operations, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The additional prompts document the existing system rather than establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the original SWE-bench reference results, Ambiguous and Stateful SWE evaluations, 15 developer profiles, and the same 17-developer field study. The added profile examples and interaction timeline do not establish expanded evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: CodeAct and RAGCodeAct remain the main comparators. v2 Section 5.2, footnote 2, additionally reports an unnamed single-agent baseline managing coding and ToM-related contexts, evaluated with Claude Sonnet 4 on N=100 and achieving 27.17% resolution. This preliminary comparison was not reported in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds a reported 100-instance preliminary baseline evaluation and a manual examination of 44 failed-but-high-satisfaction cases. Existing benchmark budgets, models, metrics, profile histories, and human-study sample sizes remain unchanged. The newly supplied common task prompt clarifies existing settings rather than establishes a protocol revision.

E4.justification: v2 extends the descriptive resolution–satisfaction analysis with correlation/regression and a 44-case qualitative audit, and adds a cross-session human-study example in Figure 7. It removes the detailed S+M disagreement breakdown. The cost/model sensitivity study and analysis of 50 human-study suggestions are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds a Pearson correlation significance result and regression reporting for resolution versus satisfaction, plus a claim that S+M differences are not statistically significant without specifying that test. Table 1 uncertainty reporting and the existing 30-case simulator-validation correlation are unchanged; no additional repeated-run or seed information is supplied.

E6.justification: v2 adds the 27.17% preliminary baseline result, r=0.74 and R^2=0.55, and the 44-case audit's 61%/39% findings. Section 5.2 corrects Stateful SWE prose from 57.4% versus 13.5% to 59.7% versus 18.1%, matching unchanged Figure 4; the introduction retains the old values. F+H values are preserved in Table 2, while detailed S+M values disappear. Main benchmark and human-acceptance charts otherwise retain their results.

T1.justification: The formal agent/context notation and mathematical substance of Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs or guarantees, and the added empirical statistical analyses do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the dual-agent user-modeling framework, Stateful SWE benchmark, improved resolution and satisfaction, and approximately 86% usefulness in the developer study. The observational framing clarifies the study's evidential limits without changing these central outcome claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets high satisfaction after failure as a process-quality or 'good-effort' reward, while emphasizing the strong overall association with resolution. It replaces v1's adverse interpretation of RAG's S+M rates with a nonsignificance qualification. The field study is explicitly characterized as observational, without a control group or support for broad causal productivity claims.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation of evaluation inputs: the shared benchmark task prompt, simulator judgment instructions and output example, three complete developer profiles, and the human-session analysis prompt appear in A.8.5 and A.10–A.12. Existing implementation settings remain. Conversely, v1's direct ToM-SWE repository link is removed; v2 links only to the OpenHands framework, without establishing that the project itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 sharpens the contrast with Ambiguous SWE's fixed simulator prompts and lack of cross-session preference tracking. It removes references including A-MEM, Zettelkasten, Nextquill, difference-aware user modeling, and Pragmatics. Many other author/year/title updates identify the same works and are bibliographic changes rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 6 to Section 2. The human-study framing and Discussion are substantially rewritten, and separate Ethics and Reproducibility statements become a consolidated Impact Statement. These changes materially reorganize the narrative beyond ordinary wording edits.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout. v1's disagreement heatmap becomes v2 Table 2 with only F+H results, while example feedback moves into prose. The cost plot gains a Pareto frontier and overhead axis, and a new cross-session timeline appears as Figure 7. Figures, tables, and listings are extensively repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scrutiny and reproducibility through concrete prompts and profiles, targeted supporting analyses, and clearer limits on the observational study. It also partially corrects numerical reporting. These gains are tempered by removal of the project link and detailed S+M results, persistent conflicting introduction scores, and an unreconciled tension between Section 6's statement that dialogue was not collected and A.12's message-analysis description. The net improvement is useful but limited.
